record.paper_title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: How does the computational efficiency of morphogenetic systems change if one imposes the recognizer-style requirement that the system must halt, in the sense that from some point onward no rule is applicable, and that exactly one distinguished output object, yes or no, is released only at the final computation step?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 How would the computational efficiency of M systems change if we insisted on halting (in the sense that no rule is applicable from a certain moment on) and releasing the object yes or no at the last step of computation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A morphogenetic system (M system) is a discrete computational model inspired by membrane computing and DNA self-assembly. Informally, an M system consists of a finite set of atomic geometric objects (tiles/proteins with shapes), a finite set of local interaction rules that govern how objects bind, unbind, transform, or move under geometric constraints in an ambient Euclidean space, and an initial configuration. Computations proceed in discrete maximally parallel steps: at each step every applicable rule is fired in parallel on a chosen multiset of objects, producing a new configuration.

Consider the standard recognizer regime imposed on M systems, defined as follows. A recognizer M system is associated with a family {Π(n)} indexed by input size n, each Π(n) receiving an input encoding of an instance of a decision problem. We say Π is a recognizer if every computation of Π satisfies:
(i) (Halting) Every computation reaches a configuration from which no rule of the system is applicable.
(ii) (Unique output) There are two distinguished objects, "yes" and "no", and in every halting computation exactly one of these two objects is released to the environment, and only at the very last computational step.

Let PMC_M denote the class of decision problems solvable in polynomial time by uniform families of recognizer M systems in the above sense, and let MC_M denote the analogous class without the recognizer-style halting and unique-output restriction (using the unrestricted notion of computational efficiency for M systems in which acceptance/rejection may be signaled by other means and rules may remain applicable indefinitely).

Determine the relationship between MC_M and PMC_M. In particular: does imposing the recognizer-style halting requirement together with the requirement that a single output object "yes" or "no" be released only at the final step strictly decrease the computational efficiency of M systems, or are the two classes equal? More generally, characterize how the class of problems solvable in polynomial time by M systems changes under these two constraints.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the overview of morphogenetic systems by Sosík and collaborators. Subsequent works on computational universality and efficiency of M systems (2021–2022) extend universality and self-healing results but do not appear to resolve the recognizer-style halting/output efficiency question. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Computational Universality and Efficiency in Morphogenetic Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study computational universality and efficiency of M systems; open theoretical problems remain.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to study M-system efficiency without resolving the recognizer-halting variant.

status_evidence.title: Self-healing Turing-universal computation in morphogenetic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Turing universality with self-healing but does not address the halting recognizer efficiency problem.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the halting-recognizer efficiency question is given.

status_evidence.title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems concerning halting and output constraints in M systems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as open.
